overview.description: Bingo Card (commonly known as Bango or Hoy!) is a high-energy social card game that blends the core mechanics of traditional Bingo with a standard deck of cards. Unlike the lottery version, every player holds a grid of actual playing cards, and a 'Caller' draws from a master deck. It is a game of pure chance and social interaction, often used as a fundraiser or party game because it can accommodate hundreds of players simultaneously with minimal equipment.
overview.deck: Standard French Packs (Multiple required for large groups)

history.origins: Developed in the mid-20th century as a more tactile and 'poker-flavored' alternative to ball-and-cage Bingo. It gained massive popularity in British working-class social clubs and American Legion halls under names like 'Hoy!' and 'Bargo'.
timeline: 1930s: Early variations appear in social clubs during the Bingo craze.
1950s: Standardized into the 'Card Grid' format widely used today.
1980s: Becomes a staple for 'Charity Nights' due to its fast pace.
Present: Popular online as '90-Ball Card Bingo' or community 'Hoy' apps.
history.evolution: The game was originally played with individual hands of 5 cards, but evolved into 9-card (3x3) or 16-card (4x4) grids to increase difficulty and prize pools.
history.cultural: In the UK, it is often called 'Hoy!' and is accompanied by traditional 'Bingo Calls' (e.g., 'Two Little Ducks' for the 2 of Hearts).

setup.deck: The Caller uses one standard 52-card deck (the 'Master Deck'). Each player is dealt a specific number of cards (usually 5 or 9) from other decks to form their personal 'Card Board'.
setup.equipment: One master deck, many player decks, markers (if cards aren't flipped), prizes.
setup.dealing: The Caller deals a 3x3 grid face-up to every player. No two players should have the exact same grid.

rules.objective: Be the first player to have all cards in your personal grid 'called' from the master deck.
rules.gameplay: 1. **The Draw**: The Caller shuffles the master deck and turns over one card at a time, announcing the rank and suit clearly (e.g., 'King of Clubs!'). 2. **Evaluation**: Any player who has that exact card in their grid turns it face down or covers it with a marker. 3. **The Shout**: Once a player has covered all cards in a row, column, or their entire grid (depending on the round's goal), they must immediately shout 'Bango!', 'Bingo!', or 'Hoy!'.
keyRules: A card only counts if you have the exact match (suit and rank).
If two people shout at the same time, the prize is usually split.
Once the Caller moves to the next card, 'missed' cards usually cannot be claimed (House dependent).

strategy.basic: Organization: Layout your cards in a consistent pattern (e.g., by suit or by color) so you can scan them instantly when a card is called.
strategy.intermediate: Listen for the Calls: If the Caller uses nicknames (like 'Legs Eleven'), memorize them to speed up your identification process.
strategy.advanced: Multi-Board Management: Advanced players will play with 2 or 3 grids at once. To do this effectively, align your grids so that similar ranks are physically close to each other on the table.
tips: In a 'Full House' game, don't get excited early. The final card is the only one that truly matters.
If playing with markers, keep them in a small bowl to avoid spilling them and losing track of your progress.

list.name: British Hoy!
list.description: Played with 9 cards (3x3). Wins are awarded for one line, then two lines, then the 'Full House'.
list.emptyOverridesReason: British Hoy! uses the same core engine; differences in prize steps and announced patterns are handled narratively, not as structured overrides yet.

list.name: Poker Bingo
list.description: A variant where 'Better' hands (like having a pair in your grid) can win smaller side-pots.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Poker Bingo adds side pots for poker-style patterns on the grid; these payout tweaks are documented in text but not yet modeled as engine overrides.

difficulty.easy: Occasionally misses a call even if they have the card. Struggles with more than one board.
difficulty.medium: Instantly identifies matches on up to 4 boards. Never misses a call.
difficulty.hard: Perfect multi-board management (up to 12 boards). Can predict 'Near-Bingo' states for every other player at the table.

considerations: AI requires a 'Scanning Speed' variable to simulate human error in loud party environments.
Must track the 'Called Deck' vs the 'Player Grid' arrays.

ante.reason: Bingo Card is a social game of matching and does not utilize a monetary or chip-based ante.

deal.reason: The distribution of grids to all players is handled automatically by the system dealer at the start.

reveal_market.reason: This is a social matching game where every player sees their own grid; no separate market exists.

buy_market.reason: Players cannot purchase or swap cards from any external area; they must succeed with their dealt grid.

buy_stock.reason: Players do not interact with the master deck; cards are only received through the Caller's announcements.

fold.reason: Participation is passive and mandatory for all players until a winner shouts the bingo condition.

check.reason: The game uses a matching and shouting structure rather than a vying structure where checking would apply.

call.reason: There is no bet to match in this game; competition is based strictly on matching cards to the grid.

bet.reason: Success is determined by pattern completion rather than through the wagering of chips or currency.

raise.reason: There are no wagering rounds in this game, so the value of the prize cannot be increased via raises.

declare.description: Shout Bingo or Hoy when the grid pattern is complete.
declare.constraints: Only available when the required pattern is matched.

reveal_hand.reason: Grids are already face up on the table; no separate reveal phase is necessary during play.

award_pot.reason: While winners receive a prize, it is managed by the caller rather than awarded through an engine action.

play_card.reason: Cards are marked or turned on the grid rather than being played to a shared trick or tableau.

draw.reason: The only cards moved are from the Master Deck by the system Caller; players do not draw cards.

discard.reason: Every card remains on the grid until the round terminates; no cards are discarded to a waste pile.

pass.reason: Players must mark their cards as they are called; passing a match is not a supported strategic action.

bid.reason: Bingo Card does not utilize a bidding system to determine the dealer or game objectives.

meld.reason: This is a matching game based on caller announcements rather than creating melds in the hand.

go_out.reason: Winning occurs through the shout declaration rather than a separate go-out engine action.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: Cards are revealed from the master deck by the caller; players do not draw from a personal stock.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Cards are marked or flipped on the grid; no separate waste or discard pile exists in the game.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Cards contribute only their rank and suit identity to the matching objective; no card has a special effect.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: The shout declaration is performed verbally when the match condition is met; no hidden tokens are used.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Bingo Card is a social matching game and does not use a capture-from-tableau fishing mechanic.
notApplicableReasons.trickConfig: The game is a pattern-matching race rather than a competitive trick-taking or climbing game.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: Goal is to complete a pattern on the grid; cards are matched, not emptied from hand as in shedding games.

customLogicNeeded: Automatic match checking for AI players.

customActions.description: Distribute unique 3x3 grids of cards to all active participants.
Caller announces the drawn card to all players.
Flip the top card of the master deck and announce it.
Cover or flip a card on the player grid that matches the announced card.
Announce the completion of the required grid pattern.
Validate that the claimed pattern is correct.
Award win to the first valid claimant.

engine.handRankingSystem: None; victory is determined by pattern completion on the card grid.
engine.deckDescription: One or more standard 52-card decks; each has four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs) and thirteen ranks. One deck is used for calling; player grids are built from the same composition. No jokers; each cell matches one specific card by suit and rank.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). Each cell on the bingo card corresponds to one exact card (suit and rank). When that card is called, the cell is marked; the first to complete a line or pattern wins.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit (ace through king). Cards are called by rank and suit (or by a standard call pattern); players match the called card to the corresponding cell on their grid. No rank hierarchy beyond exact match.
engine.dealPattern: Nine cards dealt face-up in a 3x3 grid to each player.

hero.title: BINGO CARD
hero.subtitle: The Party Classic
hero.tagline: Card by card, rank by rank. Will you be the first to shout Hoy!

synthesis.shortDescription: Bingo Card is the ultimate social game for large crowds. Using standard playing cards as your board, you must track the Caller's draw with precision. Whether it's a 3x3 grid or a high-speed 5-card dash, the rush of turning that final Ace is like no other.

prompts.human: Welcome to Bango! Check your 3x3 grid. The Caller is about to pull the first card from the deck. Keep your markers ready—when your board is full, don't forget to shout it out!
prompts.ai: Game: Bingo Card (Bango/Hoy!). Type: Social Matching. Rules: Caller pulls from master 52-card deck. Players match cards to their personal grid. First to finish pattern wins.

scoring.description: Generally prize-based or session-based score tracking.
scoring.winCondition: Completion of a pre-set pattern (Full House, Horizontal Line, 4 Corners).
scoring.splitRules: Total prize pool is divided equally by the number of simultaneous winners.

nullReasons.targetScore: No fixed target score; play by game rules.
nullReasons.cardValues: Individual cards contribute to the matching objective rather than having point values.
